title: Honey Mustard Baked Chicken Thighs
seoTitle: Honey Mustard Baked Chicken Thighs | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Crispy-skinned thighs with tangy honey-mustard glaze for ten
subtitle: Crispy-skinned thighs with tangy honey-mustard glaze for ten
description: Bone-in chicken thighs are seasoned, roasted on a wire rack until skin crisps, then brushed with honey-mustard glaze during the final minutes. Finish under the broiler for color if needed.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Honey Mustard Baked Chicken Thighs in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Season the thighs
steps.instruction: Pat chicken thighs dry. Toss with olive oil, salt, pepper, smoked paprika, and garlic powder until evenly coated. Target 165°F at the thickest part before moving to the next batch. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Roast on a rack
steps.instruction: Arrange thighs skin-side up on a wire rack over a foil-lined sheet pan. Roast at 425°F until skin crisps and internal temp reaches 155°F, about 30 minutes. Target oven/smoker temperature: 425°F.

steps.title: Build the glaze
steps.instruction: Whisk honey, Dijon, and vinegar until smooth. Taste and adjust tang with a splash more vinegar if too sweet. Plan about 3 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Glaze and finish
steps.instruction: Brush thighs with glaze and roast 8–10 more minutes until internal temp hits 165°F and glaze sets glossy. Broil 1–2 minutes for extra color if needed. Target oven/smoker temperature: 425°F.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Honey Mustard Baked Chicken Thighs onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.instruction: Rest thighs 5 minutes. Portion two per plate with pan juices spooned over and parsley scattered at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Use a leave-in probe on the largest thigh so you are not guessing on doneness.
Roast green beans on a second rack below the chicken to use oven space efficiently.
Save rendered fat from the pan for roasting potatoes on the next shift.
tonightSpread: Glazed thighs with roasted baby potatoes and steamed green beans.
Extra glaze in a squeeze bottle for crew who want more tang at the table.
leftovers: Pull meat and chop into a chicken salad with celery and light mayo.
Slice and stack on toasted bread with Swiss cheese for quick melts.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Thighs forgive timing better than breast meat and stay juicy on the hold line. One sheet pan feeds ten without standing over a grill between calls.
mealPrepNotes: Pat thighs completely dry for crisp skin. Line sheet pans with foil for fast cleanup. Glaze can be mixed ahead in squeeze bottles.
